name: usn_journal
description: Parse an NTFS change journal ($UsnJrnl:$J) into records from v2, v3 and v4 entries: name, USN, timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC with seven fractional digits, and the raw FILETIME as a decimal string), reason bits (as names and raw), the file reference and its sequence, the parent reference and its sequence, source info, security id and the attributes as names and raw. Skips the sparse front and says where the first record was and how many zero bytes it passed; says how many records it read whatever the name filter kept. What is not a record is accounted for in bytes: unrecognised_bytes after the first record (its ranges are a page, unrecognised_ranges) and prefix_unrecognised_bytes before it. A V4 record has no name: a name filter leaves V4 records out and counts them (nameless_excluded_by_filter), and include_nameless: true keeps them. Each record carries its minor_version beside version. A record of a major version this tool does not read (anything but 2, 3 and 4) that still has the shape of one (a length that is a multiple of 8, after it the end, zeros or a record that is read) is named, not only counted as unrecognised bytes: unsupported_version_records, unsupported_versions (by major version), unsupported_version_bytes and a page of them with their offset, major_version, minor_version and length (unsupported_version_list, the whole list in the file all_unsupported_version_list); their bytes are also in unrecognised_bytes. A path that is not a regular file (a FIFO, a device) is refused without being opened (not_attempted). The tool has its own clock (114 s of the manifest's 120): when it runs out the sweep stops, the pages written so far are placed and named, and the answer is partial with a status_basis that says where it stopped and how many records were read; every answer carries status and status_basis (complete only for an input read to its end), a wrong-type argument is refused as JSON (status failed), and SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with one JSON document (status failed with interrupted true, exit 128 plus the signal) and no temporary file. A result file is never replaced: the same result keeps its name, another takes the next free -n name. The skip over bytes that are not a record is inside the clock too.

limit.description: Records shown inline (default 500, 1 to 10000, an inline page size); every record is read, and when more match the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

name.description: Case-insensitive regular expression over the file name (at most 500 characters). One name is tested for at most 0.5 s; an expression that takes longer stops the sweep there (partial), so use a plain pattern

include_nameless.description: With a name filter, keep V4 (range-tracking) records, which have no name, instead of leaving them out and counting them
